_comment: ei-json baseline digest for the axibridge byte-identity guard (M17 Task 2). See ei-byte-identity.test.mjs for the regeneration procedure. Regenerated 2026-08-27. The baseline had gone STALE for the SECOND time -- it was last captured during MPVE, which landed in v1.5.0, and six releases (v1.5.0 -> v1.7.1) moved the document without anyone recapturing it. It stayed hidden because main's Linux job dies earlier, at the version-sync gate, and never reaches the Node SDK tests at all. Anchor verified rather than assumed: a v1.5.0 (7a4e8fa) build reproduces the OLD recorded digest exactly (3658140 / 4c53bf51...), which is what pins the drift window. The drift is +9,350 chars, attributed by top-level key: players +7,940, buffMap +808, personalDamageMods +369 (new in v1.7.1) and skillMap +211. The players growth is entirely inside `support` and adds NO new player-level keys -- it is the v1.6.x arcdps-parity cleanse buckets (condiCleanseArcdps, boonStripsArcdps*, condiCleanseMinions, ...). Crucially for axibridge, nothing it already consumes changed: every leaf value of the old document was compared against the new one -- 373,534 values, of which 52 moved, and all 52 are skillMap.sNNN.name going "Skill NNN" -> a real name (s1066 -> Resurrect, s30498 -> Resolve, s12854 -> Ice Whirl Combo, ...), which is the v1.6.2 SkillIDs.cs symbol rung. Zero values regressed and zero keys went missing. Determinism was confirmed per this test's own mandate: two consecutive captures at the recorded sourceCommit agree on both length and sha256. sourceCommit is now a full sha, not a branch name -- the previous entry ("mpve-pve-encounter-identification") was a branch that had been deleted after merge, so the anchor it named was unresolvable when this drift was finally investigated. || Regenerated 2026-09-01 (THIRD staleness). Drift window 14ab2f68 -> 1db5808, +736 code units (3667490 -> 3668226). Attributed by leaf-diff of a worktree build at the recorded anchor against HEAD: EXACTLY 4 keys ADDED, 0 removed, 0 changed -- skillMap.s23294 'Generic Knockdown', s23295 'Generic Knockback and Pull', s23296 'Generic Float', s23299 'Generic Control Effect From Buff'. These are the arcdps generic control effect ids that v1.10.0's CC attribution lane started naming; purely additive, and nothing axibridge already consumes moved. The anchor was VERIFIED not assumed: a build at 14ab2f68 reproduces the previous recorded pair (3667490 / 0310eaa9...) exactly. The blocks.focus merge (47ca3c4) is NOT implicated -- a build at its first parent 1db5808 produces the same 3668226 / 1a91803b... as HEAD, byte for byte. Same hiding mechanism as last time: main's Linux job died at the version-sync gate for every release from v1.8.0 to v1.10.2 and never reached the Node SDK tests, so four releases' worth of CI never ran this guard. Determinism reconfirmed: two consecutive captures agree on length and sha256.
